API inventory completeness remains pending.

One generic Rust implementation now delegates primitive operations to project-owned scalar policies. Narrow integer squared products are promoted before summing and narrowing; magnitude takes sqrt before the final element cast. Normalize uses division followed by assignment without requiring DivAssign. Floating abs bits and floating JSON promotion match the pinned native fixture. C++ constexpr evaluation, unsupported element types, overflow/out-of-range undefined cases, generic layout and reentrant aliasing remain unproven; see porting/audits/vector-component-contracts.json. D1 review 2026-10-15 (docs/tkernel-rust-refactoring-plan.md): the differences this note leaves open are C++ language properties with no Rust counterpart: noexcept termination, ABI and vtable layout, constexpr evaluation, implicit conversions, template instantiation over arbitrary element types and C++ std::hash specialisations; native undefined behaviour (overflow, out-of-range or invalid raw owners), which has no native result to reproduce; aliased or const_cast mutation that Rust borrowing rules forbid, so no Rust caller can produce it. D1 makes none of them a parity obligation, and the behaviour a Rust caller can observe is covered by the cited native evidence and tests, so the row is implemented.

Mat4::map_ref_mut borrows the caller's flat column-major array as a complete Mat4 (repr(transparent) over the same storage), so the whole NCollection_Mat4 member surface reads and writes the caller storage in place, as the native Map reinterpret_cast does; tests/matrix_alias_method_contracts.rs checks determinant, transpose, data pointer identity and the zero-sized case. The element-only MatrixView adapters (Mat4::map/map_mut) stay as Rust conveniences. Former partial note: Safe borrowed MatrixViewMut preserves native column-major alias read/write behavior for a caller-borrowed [T; 16] buffer. It intentionally exposes only element and slice access, not the full NCollection_Mat4 method surface, and Rust borrowing forbids aliases that violate exclusive access. Native probe and limitations: porting/runtime-evidence/tkernel-matrix-map.md.

One generic Rust implementation now delegates primitive operations to project-owned scalar policies. Narrow integer squared products are promoted before summing and narrowing; magnitude takes sqrt before the final element cast. Normalize uses division followed by assignment without requiring DivAssign. Floating abs bits and floating JSON promotion match the pinned native fixture. C++ constexpr evaluation, unsupported element types, overflow/out-of-range undefined cases, generic layout and reentrant aliasing remain unproven; see porting/audits/vector-component-contracts.json. D1 review 2026-10-15 (docs/tkernel-rust-refactoring-plan.md): the differences this note leaves open are C++ language properties with no Rust counterpart: noexcept termination, ABI and vtable layout, constexpr evaluation, implicit conversions, template instantiation over arbitrary element types and C++ std::hash specialisations; native undefined behaviour (overflow, out-of-range or invalid raw owners), which has no native result to reproduce; aliased or const_cast mutation that Rust borrowing rules forbid, so no Rust caller can produce it. D1 makes none of them a parity obligation, and the behaviour a Rust caller can observe is covered by the cited native evidence and tests, so the row is implemented.

Explicit Poly mapping. Transient classes keep their fields behind one lock, so members take &self and changes are seen through every Handle; references to internal arrays become copies or closures run under the lock; pointers to coherent triangles and links become indices; C++ out parameters become returned values except Poly::Intersect, whose partially written outputs are native; exceptions become Failure errors carrying the offending value.

Rust returns a safe shared Array1 view that detaches on first write. The native const overload returns a mutable alias over the LocalArray buffer, so writes through that view mutate the original even when the LocalArray is const. Rust intentionally does not emulate that aliasing. See tools/oracle/tkernel_local_array_const_to_array1.md. D1 review 2026-10-15 (docs/tkernel-rust-refactoring-plan.md): the difference this note leaves open is a write through a view obtained from a const object, a const_cast alias that Rust borrowing forbids, so no Rust caller can produce it; the non-const ToArray1 overload is the writable alias. D1 makes it no parity obligation, so the row is implemented.

Borrowed insertion copies the referenced key and/or value after reserving and hashing, before lookup, on both misses and hits. Hash/copy/equality order and primitive values match the pinned native fixture in porting/audits/flat-borrowed-insertion.json. Rust Clone models copies; C++ move/assignment/destruction hooks, physical slot layout, exception unwinding, and arbitrary aliasing remain unproven. D1 review 2026-10-15 (docs/tkernel-rust-refactoring-plan.md): the differences this note leaves open are C++ copy/move/assignment hooks of the element or policy type, std::move_if_noexcept relocation and the partial state a throwing copy leaves (class B2); raw node/slot addresses, physical layout and pointer identity of internal storage (class B5); a throwing destructor or the native termination it causes (class B1); aliased or const_cast mutation that Rust borrowing rules forbid, so no Rust caller can produce it. D1 makes none of them a parity obligation, and the behaviour a Rust caller can observe is covered by the cited native evidence and tests, so the row is implemented.

Borrowed insertion copies the referenced key and/or value after reserving and hashing, before lookup, on both misses and hits. Hash/copy/equality order and primitive values match the pinned native fixture in porting/audits/flat-borrowed-insertion.json. Rust Clone models copies; C++ move/assignment/destruction hooks, physical slot layout, exception unwinding, and arbitrary aliasing remain unproven. D1 review 2026-10-15 (docs/tkernel-rust-refactoring-plan.md): the differences this note leaves open are C++ copy/move/assignment hooks of the element or policy type, std::move_if_noexcept relocation and the partial state a throwing copy leaves (class B2); raw node/slot addresses, physical layout and pointer identity of internal storage (class B5); a throwing destructor or the native termination it causes (class B1); aliased or const_cast mutation that Rust borrowing rules forbid, so no Rust caller can produce it. D1 makes none of them a parity obligation, and the behaviour a Rust caller can observe is covered by the cited native evidence and tests, so the row is implemented.

Traversal of live nodes is covered by first_node()/OrderedNodeRef::order_next.

Manual NCollection member mapping; the virtual NCollection_BaseAllocator interface is one shared BaseAllocator handle whose policy (common, heap, incremental, accumulating, aligned) is chosen at construction, so every subclass override maps to the same BaseAllocator method. allocate_raw/allocate_optimal_raw return the raw address (None where upstream returns NULL or throws Standard_OutOfMemory) and the unsafe free_raw releases it; BaseAllocator::allocate returns RAII-owned zeroed bytes whose Drop performs the Free. Addresses come from Rust's global allocator with a malloc-style size header; policies are compared with OCCT by the ncoll_allocators differential probe. The accumulating policy is NCollection_AccAllocator's: sizes rounded to 4, blocks keyed by address / block size and filled downwards, oversize requests in a dedicated block, a scan of the 15 previous blocks before a new one, an emptied block freed (or, when it is the only one, reallocated to the default size), and Free of an address no block owns, or of a block with no live allocation, raising Standard_ProgramError with the native message. A zero block size, which divides by zero natively, is refused with Standard_ProgramError.
Excluded: C++ destructor. Rust releases owned state through Drop glue; there is no callable counterpart to map. The engine's Drop frees every block.

Starts with errno 0 and portable code 0 on every host.

Linux/macOS: the native errno x OSD_WhoAmI switch (SUN/IRIX4/AIX arms are not compiled natively either), stores the ERR_* code and returns Err(OSD_OSDError) with the native text, keeping the 'Unknowm' spelling and the ELOOP arm that leaves ERR_SURPRISE; Ok when nothing failed. Windows: prints 'Error ( <class> )' (32-wchar truncation kept) plus the message to stderr and returns Ok. Differential probe osd_error covers every named errno from every class.

Stores errno, the raw OSD_WhoAmI (unknown values keep the default arms) and the message; on Windows also maps the Win32 code through the file/directory/file-node table then the common table (windows_error_code, tested on every host).
The portable ERR_* code: Unix sets it only in Perror, Windows in SetValue.

Linux/macOS order kept (SetFloatingSignal, record the mode, then handlers unless AsIs). Ported: the mode record, the floating-point traps, the SIGINT handler that arms ControlBreak (SetUnhandled restores a previous non-default SIGINT handler), and Unset restoring SIG_DFL on all eight managed signals. Rust cannot unwind or long-jump out of a signal handler (or translate Windows structured exceptions into panics), so the handlers that turn SIGSEGV, SIGFPE, SIGILL, SIGBUS, SIGHUP, SIGQUIT, SIGSYS (and SEH) into OSD_SIG*/OSD_Exception_* C++ exceptions are not installed. Windows: records the mode, honours CSF_DEBUG_MODE (message, stack trace length 10 when 0), installs/removes the console Ctrl-C/Ctrl-Break handler (MessageBeep not ported; other console events exit(254)), clears the break flag, then SetThreadLocalSignal; the unhandled-exception filter and signal() translators are not installed. SignalState::set_signal with an injected SignalHost is the testable form. Probes osd_signal/osd_ctrl_break.

Forwards to SetSignal(OSD_SignalMode_Set, floating), with the same partial port. Rust cannot unwind or long-jump out of a signal handler (or translate Windows structured exceptions into panics), so the handlers that turn SIGSEGV, SIGFPE, SIGILL, SIGBUS, SIGHUP, SIGQUIT, SIGSYS (and SEH) into OSD_SIG*/OSD_Exception_* C++ exceptions are not installed.

Unix/macOS: exactly SetFloatingSignal(floating), as natively (mode ignored). Windows: the _set_se_translator part is not ported (SE translation raises C++ exceptions); the floating-point part is. Probe osd_thread_signal.

Linux/glibc (x86, x86-64, AArch64): feclearexcept(FE_ALL_EXCEPT) then feenable/fedisableexcept(FE_INVALID|FE_DIVBYZERO|FE_OVERFLOW) for the calling thread, as natively; other Unix targets (macOS, musl) do nothing, as the native #else branch. Windows: _fpreset, _clearfp, _controlfp(0 or mask, _EM_INVALID|_EM_DENORMAL|_EM_ZERODIVIDE|_EM_OVERFLOW) (not observed on a Windows host). Probe osd_floating.
Process-wide atomic, AsIs by default, set by every SetSignal. Host independent.
Linux/glibc: (fegetexcept() & mask) != 0; macOS/other Unix: false, as natively; Windows: a mask bit cleared in _controlfp(0, 0). Probes osd_signal/osd_floating.

Default Osd::sec_sleep dispatches to NativeSleeper: Unix calls usleep(seconds*1000*1000) and ignores its return, so EINTR ends the sleep early; Windows calls Sleep(seconds*1000) ms (cross-compiled, not runtime tested). Osd::sec_sleep_with(custom, ...) remains injectable and defaults to the legacy Duration conversion. Native signed overflow for large seconds is undefined; parity is claimed only for inputs whose int multiplication is defined.

Default Osd::milli_sec_sleep dispatches to NativeSleeper: Unix calls usleep(milliseconds*1000) and ignores its return, so EINTR ends the sleep early; Windows calls Sleep(milliseconds) directly (cross-compiled, not runtime tested). Osd::milli_sec_sleep_with(custom, ...) remains injectable and defaults to the legacy Duration conversion. Native signed overflow for large millisecond values is undefined; parity is claimed only for inputs whose int multiplication is defined.

No name and a null handle. Unix DlOpen(NULL) selects the main program; native Windows converts the missing name through TCollection_ExtendedString and may raise. Rust returns false for that null-name case. Windows calls are implemented behind Win32 bindings but runtime-unverified; see tools/oracle/tkernel_osd_shlib_windows.md.

The byte constructor preserves arbitrary non-NUL bytes and native first-NUL prefix semantics; valid UTF-8 callers retain the named convenience method. Null name is Option::None; native leaves its name uninitialized and Windows conversion may fail. Unix behavior is covered by tkernel_osd_shlib_bytes. Windows loader is implemented and fake-tested, but native runtime is unverified (tools/oracle/tkernel_osd_shlib_windows.md).

The byte setter preserves arbitrary non-NUL bytes, truncates at the first NUL, and treats null as no-op; string setter is a UTF-8 convenience. Replacing an old native name leaks that allocation; Rust replaces it safely. Unix bytes are covered by tkernel_osd_shlib_bytes. Windows loader is implemented and fake-tested, but runtime-unverified; native Destroy leaves a dangling name pointer while Rust clears it safely (tools/oracle/tkernel_osd_shlib_windows.md).
Returns the stored native bytes, including non-UTF-8 names; None for a null name. The string convenience name() returns None for invalid UTF-8.

Unix dlopen with RTLD_LAZY or RTLD_NOW; byte names preserve arbitrary non-NUL bytes and first-NUL semantics. Windows follows GetModuleHandleW cache then LoadLibraryExW with LOAD_WITH_ALTERED_SEARCH_PATH; LoadMode is ignored natively. Fake-tested and Windows GNU cross-compiled, but native runtime unverified; null-name exception behavior remains different. See tools/oracle/tkernel_osd_shlib_windows.md.

Unix dlclose; takes &mut self to remember close. Native dlclose(NULL) and double closes are undefined; Rust ignores them. Windows calls FreeLibrary but keeps native handle state; Rust tracks closed state and safely rejects subsequent lookup. Windows fake-tested and cross-compiled, native runtime unverified (tools/oracle/tkernel_osd_shlib_windows.md).

Unix dlerror bytes are copied before the next loader call and consumed; None when no error. Windows passes persistent 1024-unit and 1024-byte buffers directly to FormatMessageW/WideCharToMultiByte and ignores both return codes, retaining any writes made before failure. Rust serializes access with a mutex; fake tests cover partial writes and capacity boundaries. Native Windows runtime remains unverified (tools/oracle/tkernel_osd_shlib_windows.md).

Forgets the name and handle without unloading the library on Unix. Windows native Destroy frees the name but leaves its pointer dangling and keeps the handle value; Rust safely clears its owned name and preserves the handle field, while closed-state tracking prevents later lookup. Windows runtime is unverified; see tools/oracle/tkernel_osd_shlib_windows.md.
Excluded: C++ destructor that calls Destroy. Rust drop glue releases the name and, like Destroy, never unloads the library.

Figures come from the injectable MemInfoSource (NativeMemInfo: glibc mallinfo2, /proc/<pid>/status, macOS task_info + malloc_zone_statistics). Linux: heap from mallinfo2 uordblks (0 without glibc), then VmSize/VmRSS/VmHWM and VmData+VmStk (atol kB x 1024, size_t wrap) in the native else-if order, skipped when none of those counters is active; swap counters stay unknown. macOS: virtual, resident and malloc bytes, all three stored when any is active (native quirk). Native labels, int(ValueMiB) and the peak suffixes; only active, known counters print. Named to_text (it returns AsciiString). Every host.

Integer division by 1024*1024; usize::MAX when inactive or unknown. Every host.
bytes / (1024.0*1024.0); -1.0 when inactive or unknown. Every host.
ToString of a freshly updated native MemInfo (see Update for the Windows gap).
Always true: this profile builds without TBB (USE_TBB=OFF), so OCCT threads are the only backend, as in the native non-TBB build on every platform. Probe osd_nproc.
Ignored, as in the native non-TBB build on every platform. Probe osd_nproc.

Computed once and cached. Linux and macOS: sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN) (online processors, not the affinity mask; -1 on error, as natively; the Android cpu-mask branch is not a target). Windows: GetSystemInfo dwNumberOfProcessors (a 64-bit Rust process never takes the WOW64 GetNativeSystemInfo branch). Probe osd_nproc compares the Linux value.

The iterator pair becomes one Rust Iterator (Send items, so iter_mut() shares mutable elements); forced or nbItems == 1 runs sequentially in the caller and lets a panic unwind unchanged; otherwise forEachOcct: a Launcher of min(nbItems, NbDefaultThreadsToLaunch) (-1: pool default) on the default pool hands items out under a mutex (OSD_Parallel_Threads Range). Pooled failures return Standard_ProgramError. Probe osd_foreach. Host independent: std::thread on every platform.

Named for_range (`for` is a Rust keyword). Forced or single-index ranges run `for (it = begin; it != end; ++it)` in the caller (wrapping, as natively); otherwise a Launcher(DefaultPool, end - begin) Perform. Pooled failures return Standard_ProgramError. Probe osd_for. Host independent: std::thread on every platform.
No function, no thread, id 0, priority 0. Host independent.
OSD_ThreadFunction (void* (*)(void*)) is `fn(usize) -> usize`: the opaque pointer-sized argument and result travel as usize. Host independent.

Copies function and priority, detaches its own thread, then shares the other's thread and id. Linux/macOS keep the pthread handle semantics: copies share one thread; the first Wait joins it and later Waits of any copy fail; Detach of any copy (also by dropping it) makes it unjoinable for all. Windows natively duplicates the handle per copy, so there a copy's Detach/destruction does not affect the others; the Rust port keeps the pthread sharing on every host (documented deviation for Windows).
Linux/macOS: stores the value without effect, as the native pthread branch. Windows: SetThreadPriority on the running thread (and at Run), through windows-sys.
Detaches the current thread, then stores the function. Host independent.

False without a function or when the system refuses the thread; detaches the previous thread first; records the pthread_t (Linux/macOS) or Win32 thread id (Windows) as GetId. The stack size is honoured on Windows only (positive values), ignored by the pthread build as natively. Probe osd_thread/osd_thread_copy.

Drops the JoinHandle (pthread_detach) and clears the id. Linux/macOS keep the pthread handle semantics: copies share one thread; the first Wait joins it and later Waits of any copy fail; Detach of any copy (also by dropping it) makes it unjoinable for all. Windows natively duplicates the handle per copy, so there a copy's Detach/destruction does not affect the others; the Rust port keeps the pthread sharing on every host (documented deviation for Windows).

Joins; false when nothing runs or the thread was already joined/detached through a copy. Probe osd_thread. Linux/macOS keep the pthread handle semantics: copies share one thread; the first Wait joins it and later Waits of any copy fail; Detach of any copy (also by dropping it) makes it unjoinable for all. Windows natively duplicates the handle per copy, so there a copy's Detach/destruction does not affect the others; the Rust port keeps the pthread sharing on every host (documented deviation for Windows).

The output pointer becomes Option<usize>: None is the native false with a null result. Rust deviation: a panicking thread function makes Wait fail (a throwing native thread terminates the process). Probe osd_thread.

Joins if the thread ends within the timeout (negative counts as 0; natively an invalid or past timespec also fails). Linux: pthread_timedjoin_np natively, a timed condition wait here. macOS: natively no pthread_timedjoin_np, the timeout is ignored and the call joins; the port does the same. Windows: WaitForSingleObject(timeout) natively, the timed condition wait here. Probe osd_thread_timed.
The pthread_t (Linux/macOS) or Win32 thread id (Windows) recorded by Run; 0 when nothing runs. Probe osd_thread_timed checks it equals Current() inside the thread.
pthread_self() on Linux/macOS, GetCurrentThreadId() on Windows, as usize (Standard_ThreadId).

functor(threadIndex, index) for each index handed out by a shared atomic counter (wrapping fetch_add, `it < end`); the caller runs its share synchronously, then waits for every woken worker. The abstract base maps to the FileSystem trait; implementing it is the Rust constructor. std::istream/std::ostream/std::streambuf shared pointers become the project-owned SharedIStream/SharedOStream/SharedStreamBuf (Arc<Mutex<dyn IStream/OStream/StreamBuf>>) with the libstdc++ sentry and state rules; the handle is FileSystemHandle (Arc<dyn FileSystem>) because the crate Handle<T> projects to one concrete type while file systems are an open interface. Mutating virtuals take &self and lock internally (the default file system is shared process-wide). Exceptions (Standard_ASSERT_RAISE) become Err(Standard_ProgramError) with the native message; the assert names the source basename where the native text carries the absolute build path. Host independent: std::fs gives the same behavior on Linux, Windows and macOS (Unicode paths reach the native wide-character APIs on Windows).

FILE* becomes Option<std::fs::File> (None for NULL). Linux converts the name to UTF-8 and parses the mode as glibc fopen does ('r'/'w'/'a' then up to six modifiers: '+' update, 'x' exclusive, others ignored; a write-only append stream starts at the end). The extern "C" OSD_OpenFile(const char*, const char*) is open_file_utf8. Windows: _wfopen accepts the MSVC mode letters (e.g. 't', 'ccs='); the Rust parser keeps the glibc rules on every host. Probe osd_fs_fopen (22 modes).
stat().st_ctime in seconds, 0 when stat fails. Linux/macOS: status-change time (MetadataExt::ctime); Windows: _wstat64 st_ctime is the creation time, read from Metadata::created. Probe osd_fs_ctime.

The descriptor becomes Option<std::fs::File> (None for -1). Native quirk kept: any mode with out is O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC (+O_APPEND with app) even with in or without trunc, since O_RDONLY is 0; no out opens read-only; created files get 0600. Windows: _wsopen_s with the same flags; its text-mode translation (no binary) is not reproduced. Probe osd_fs_fd covers all 64 modes.

std::filebuf is FileBuffer: the libstdc++ openmode table (binary ignored, invalid combinations refused, ate seeks to the end), glibc's end start for write-only append, unbuffered reads and the libstdc++ put area (pending small writes; pubseekoff(0, cur) adds them to the file offset). Windows/MinGW open the same modes through std. Probe osd_fs_filebuf covers all 64 modes.

The template over std::ifstream/ofstream/fstream becomes FileStream (input/output/input_output adds in/out/nothing); open failure sets failbit, success clears the state. Probe osd_fs_fstream. Host independent: std::fs gives the same behavior on Linux, Windows and macOS (Unicode paths reach the native wide-character APIs on Windows).

UTF-8 name overload of the FileStream open (Windows converts it to UTF-16 first, as std does). Probe osd_fs_fstream. Host independent: std::fs gives the same behavior on Linux, Windows and macOS (Unicode paths reach the native wide-character APIs on Windows).
Enumeration with native declaration order as i32 discriminants; `ALL` lists the values and `from_raw` inverts `as i32`. Host independent.

The extern "C" overload: fopen of a UTF-8 name; FILE* becomes Option<std::fs::File> (None for NULL), with the glibc mode parsing of open_file. Windows: native _wfopen after UTF-8 to UTF-16 conversion accepts the MSVC mode letters; the Rust parser keeps the glibc rules on every host. Probe osd_fs_fopen.

Excluded: OSD_WNT.hxx is the Windows-only C helper layer of the _WIN32 OSD build (OSD_WNT.cxx compiles only under _WIN32, and the header includes <windows.h>). It hands out raw Win32 security objects (PSECURITY_DESCRIPTOR, PSID, PACL, ACEs) with manual Alloc/Free pairs and directory move/copy callbacks, and only the Windows branches of OSD_File, OSD_FileNode, OSD_Directory, OSD_Protection and OSD_Process call it. The Rust port reaches Windows through std/windows-sys inside those classes and does not export this raw-pointer C layer; on Linux/macOS the header does not exist in the native build either.

The lock writes the storage owned plane, an atomic bit plane, through the shared attached graph; the parent and child walks can raise as the explorers do, so the members that walk return Result, and the noexcept callbacks stop walking on an error.

Partial IntTools_EdgeFace port. Public state accessors and bounded line/plane Perform paths are present. Native-backed Rust fixtures cover line/plane crossing, quick coincidence, line/cylinder tangency and circle/plane tangency (tools/oracle/tkbo_edge_face.md); tangent numeric fields match at absolute tolerance 1e-12. Helper tests cover CheckTouchVertex and line/plane HInter fallback. Seven additional native lifecycle snapshots check 49 state fields exactly across repeated Perform, invalid edges, fuzzy clamping and context reset. Supplemental evidence does not map new legacy declarations. Broader curve/surface families, arbitrary lifecycle histories, and additional bounded HInter fallback cases remain unproven. Touch stages now use transformed geometric adaptors, with native curve intervals and distinct face/underlying surface bounds; a translated tangency replay also passes. Reviewed line by line against IntTools_EdgeFace.cxx (2026-10-15): constructor defaults, CheckData codes 2/3, criteria from the BSpline/Bezier tolerance ratio, IsCoincident (23 or 2 segments, 1% range shrink, RealToInt thresholds, classification gating, 0.5 ratio), DistanceFunction with IsEqDistance on cylinder/cone/torus and error code 4, MakeType, CheckTouch (face-bound Extrema, HInter fallback keeping the last point in range, boundary and middle candidates), CheckTouchVertex (surface-bound Extrema, 8e-5/9e-5 end tolerances) and the line/cylinder and non-coplanar circle/plane passes. Fixed in this review: IsProjectable now samples IntTools_Tools::IntermediatePoint (0.43213918) of each BeanFace range instead of its middle (regression test projectable_ranges_are_sampled_at_the_native_intermediate_point). The BeanFace solver that produces the ranges keeps its own partial rows; these EdgeFace members are faithful, so the rows are implemented.

Excluded: DEFINE_STANDARD_ALLOC generates this class-specific operator, which returns one object's memory through Standard::Free. Rust has no per-type allocation or placement operator: a value lives inline, in a Box, a Handle or a collection, and its storage comes from and returns to the owner's allocator when it is created and dropped. A Rust port of the class needs no counterpart; no behavior is lost.

Exposes the protected active-and-known predicate through the existing shared implementation. Zero is valid; usize::MAX is unknown; disabling retains the sample for reactivation; Clear invalidates samples. Native Linux derived-class transition receipt plus deterministic injected-source tests. This predicate does not change the separately partial platform-specific Update implementation. See porting/audits/osd-mem-info-has-value.json.

Protected report operation over an explicitly supplied nullable composite; preserves child traversal at selected gravity, C-string keys, and native live-list append/unlink semantics during callbacks. Public dump/send routes release the report-state mutex before callback invocation. Native derived-class oracle and supplemental tests: porting/audits/message-report-composite-hooks.json. Native invalidation by deleting the current list node is outside the defined iterator domain.

Exact partial adapter, not full C++ template parity. Rust M is inverse native IsConstant; const construction/value policies use M=false and writable policies M=true. Explicit owner arguments preserve valid native identity domains; reference and explicit callback accessors share dispatch and Result propagation. Callbacks preserve returned R without Clone/Default bounds but do not automatically emulate arbitrary C++ user copy/move hooks. Signed arithmetic is credited only on native defined conversion/non-overflow domains; no ABI/noexcept/invalid raw owner claim. See porting/audits/base-map-indexed-method-tail.json. D1 review 2026-10-15 (docs/tkernel-rust-refactoring-plan.md): the differences this note leaves open are C++ copy/move/assignment hooks of the element or policy type, std::move_if_noexcept relocation and the partial state a throwing copy leaves (class B2); C++ language properties with no Rust counterpart: noexcept termination, ABI and vtable layout, constexpr evaluation, implicit conversions, template instantiation over arbitrary element types and C++ std::hash specialisations; aliased or const_cast mutation that Rust borrowing rules forbid, so no Rust caller can produce it; native undefined behaviour (overflow, out-of-range or invalid raw owners), which has no native result to reproduce; raw node/slot addresses, physical layout and pointer identity of internal storage (class B5). D1 makes none of them a parity obligation, and the behaviour a Rust caller can observe is covered by the cited native evidence and tests, so the row is implemented.

OSD_Function becomes SymbolAddress (NonNull<c_void>), None for a missing symbol; callers transmute to the real signature. Byte names preserve non-NUL bytes and truncate at NUL. Unix null handle is RTLD_DEFAULT on glibc. Windows uses GetProcAddress and is fake-tested/cross-compiled, not runtime-verified. Rust rejects lookup after close instead of using native dangling handle state; see tools/oracle/tkernel_osd_shlib_windows.md.

Copy constructor through Assign. Linux/macOS keep the pthread handle semantics: copies share one thread; the first Wait joins it and later Waits of any copy fail; Detach of any copy (also by dropping it) makes it unjoinable for all. Windows natively duplicates the handle per copy, so there a copy's Detach/destruction does not affect the others; the Rust port keeps the pthread sharing on every host (documented deviation for Windows).

Manual NCollection member mapping; NCollection_UBTreeFiller is UBTreeFiller<'t, T, B>, borrowing the tree mutably. The pending items live in a DynamicArray of 256-item blocks and are drawn with a bit-exact std::mt19937 seeded 5489 (full random: draw % i; otherwise i - draw % i - 1, the drawn slot taking the last live item). CheckTree's Sprintf text, including glibc's -nan for a one-leaf tree, is compared with the native filler by the differential probe. The destructor has an observable effect (it fills pending items), so it maps to the Drop implementation. Native virtual Add dispatch retained for UBTree and EBTree via BoundingTreeInsertion; editable index survives Fill and destructor flushing.

Native protected layer grouping and debug cleanup at OCCT 3d097a0. Layer order follows depth-clear/depth-write transitions, clears stale map entries first, and retains a partial prefix on failure. Cleanup follows live sequence links without callback locks, erases/clears/removes every structure, clears the sequence, then updates a non-null view. Ten new direct tests and 2656 new numeric cases also compare private picked-point/depth-tolerance and per-entity frustum/cache helpers against actual native member functions. Native null-camera rectangular rebuilding is undefined and archived separately; no claim of parity for that dereference. See docs/v3d-design.md.

tests.reason: The test asserts std::is_move_constructible<BRepAlgoAPI_BuilderAlgo>::value is false, a C++ type trait. Every Rust value can be moved (a bitwise move that ends the source binding), so no Rust test can check that the type is not movable; the related copy properties are translated as not_copy_constructible/not_copy_assignable.

The test asserts std::is_move_assignable<BRepAlgoAPI_BuilderAlgo>::value is false, a C++ type trait. Every Rust value can be move-assigned (a bitwise move that ends the source binding), so no Rust test can check that the type is not movable; the related copy properties are translated as not_copy_constructible/not_copy_assignable.
